newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez says Brazil deal "not great".
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez says Brazil deal "not great".

text.p: The Argentine-Brazilian trade dispute over Brazil's new import financing limits is "on hold" until they meet again June 30, said Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez in an interview published Monday.

Speaking to Clarin newspaper, he said this weekend's summit between Argentine President Carlos Menem and Brazil's Fernando Henrique Cardoso produced a deal that was "not great, but the best that was possible."
Menem failed to get Brazil to reverse moves announced last month which put new limits on import financing of less than 360 days, effectively forcing importers to pay in cash.
But he said Brazil did agree to give its Mercosur customs union partners Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay advance warning of trade measures in future to "avoid surprises."

Menem also clinched a deal allowing carmakers in Argentina to export some 110,000 vehicles to Brazil over the next three years -- a concession to Argentine complaints about tax breaks for carmakers setting up in Brazil's poor northeast.
The import financing move angered Brazil's Mercosur partners, who called it "protectionist" and complained that they were not consulted beforehand.
Brazil reacted by agreeing at the beginning of April to change the rules for the Mercosur, a deal to last until July 31 while more long-term solutions are sought.

"If we hadn't done anything, after July 31 we would return to the situation of having to sell to Brazil under the system of payments in cash," said Fernandez, who hopes to find a common Mercosur import financing regime by that deadline.
"The issue of restrictions on imports is on hold. We shall meet again June 30 to elaborate a common trade financing regime to be applied after July 31," said the minister.
Fernandez said he was sympathetic to Brazil's arguments that its widening trade deficit forced it to take measures "to avoid financial speculation that encouraged extra imports."
He said it was unclear what impact the import limitations would have on the Argentine economy.

"We have our doubts about whether it's an anti-trade or anti-finance measure. No Argentine producer has come to tell us that a deal has fallen through because they can't get financing for more than 89 days," said Fernandez.
